subject: Post-call: tokenstorm, stream-windowing, and SLA split — pilot next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <alex@fastcart.ai>, Devon Park <devon@fastcart.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: tokenstorm, stream-windowing, and SLA split — pilot next steps

Thanks for the detailed call this morning — good alignment on product goals and the primary risk areas. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can size the pilot properly: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct anything off):
- Baseline steady traffic: ~45 QPS average during business hours, ~100 tokens/request average (approx 4.5k tokens/sec).
- Sustained high windows: ~200 QPS for 3–5 minute windows, ~150 tokens/request (~30k tokens/sec).
- Short crest/"tokenstorm": ~1,200 QPS for ~20–30s with ~250 tokens/request (\u2248 300k tokens/sec) — this is your primary capacity and SLO risk.
- Streaming paths (live UI assistant): up to 1,000 concurrent streams; typical emit rate ~10 tokens/sec/stream (~10k tokens/sec) with low per-turn latency needs.
- Latency targets: 95th <= 300ms for non-streaming API; streaming incremental token latency <= 250ms; system must avoid 5xxs during crests.

Redwood sizing notes / hypotheses for pilot: 
- Pilot should include a dedicated capacity pool sized for crest buffering + steady-state: recommend starting with a 4-GPU pool (A100-equivalent) with autoscale headroom for short crests.
- Aggressive KV prefix caching for top 25% prompt shapes to cut token compute in half for repeated flows.
- Configure a short token-bucket rate limiter per-account to avoid noisy-neighbor amplification during crests; allow queued burst window of 45s.
- Streaming concurrency: reserve a separate streaming-capacity lane (1 GPU equivalent) so incremental token latency stays consistent.

Immediate asks from us so we can finalize the sizing proposal (attached draft):
1) Can you share a 24-hour sample trace (ingress timestamps, request length in tokens, endpoint type — streaming vs non-streaming)? We referenced s3 link below — a small sample will do.
2) Confirm crest duration: is 20–30s the right ballpark or do you see longer tails (60–90s)?
3) Any hard latency SLA penalties or downstream timeouts we should know about?
4) Would you be open to a short canary that routes 5% of traffic to a cached variant to validate cache hit uplift?

Next steps & timeline:
- We’ll update the sizing proposal with your trace and return a detailed slot-level plan (today + 24h).
- Scheduling: propose a pilot start on Mon 2027-10-04 (2-week pilot).

Attachments: fastcart_traffic_snapshot.csv (sample), redwood_sizing_proposal_v1.xlsx (draft), streaming_trace_sample.jsonl (example format).

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai

From: Alex Martin <alex@fastcart.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Park <devon@fastcart.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: tokenstorm, stream-windowing, and SLA split — pilot next steps

Thanks, Soojin — this is great. A few clarifications inline: 

- Crest duration: median crest is ~25s but we do see tails up to 75s during marketing bursts (we forgot to mention the campaign-driven spikes). Expect 2–3 campaign periods per day during launches.
- Streaming: the 1,000 concurrent figure is correct for our EU peak; US peak is closer to 800. Streams are user-initiated and frequently overlap with non-stream requests (same user sessions).
- Latency SLAs: our product enforces a 95th <= 350ms at the API layer — anything above triggers user-side fallbacks. We do not have contractual penalties yet but we consider anything >350ms as unacceptable.

Attached is a 6-hour slice we pulled (s3://fastcart-prod/logs/20270921-sample.gz). The CSV has columns: ts, endpoint, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms, concurrent_streams. Let us know if you need a different window.

We can commit to the 5% canary for cache validation. Pilot start of Oct 4 works for us.

—Alex
Alex Martin
Head of Platform, FastCart
alex@fastcart.ai

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <alex@fastcart.ai>, Devon Park <devon@fastcart.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: tokenstorm, stream-windowing, and SLA split — pilot next steps

Appreciate the log slice, Alex — that makes the pilot sizing straightforward. A few operational decisions we recommend before kickoff so the pilot is productive: 

Action items (internal + ask of FastCart):
- FastCart: confirm whether campaign spikes are predictable (scheduled) or unpredictable. If scheduled, we can pre-warm capacity to avoid queueing.
- Redwood: we’ll provision a 4-GPU baseline + 2-GPU burst buffer (auto-unlock for up to 90s) for the pilot; that maps to roughly the 300k tokens/sec crest headroom you described.
- FastCart: share the list of the top 10 prompt shapes (we’ll precompute KV-cache fingerprints).
- Redwood: enable a streaming-only lane (1 GPU equivalent) with a reserved concurrency of 1,000 streams for the pilot.
- Instrumentation: we’ll enable token-level tracing and a per-route 95/99ms histogram to prove tail behavior; please confirm you’re OK with temporary retention for pilot diagnostics.

Sizing rationale (short): 
- Crest buffer sizing: 2x of observed crest to avoid immediate autoscale churn; this buys ~90s of headroom allowing queued requests to drain with minimal 5xxs.
- Cache uplift: for repeated prompts we expect 30–50% token compute reduction (depends on shape reuse).

Deliverables by Sep 24 (internal): updated redwood_sizing_proposal_v2.xlsx and a short runbook for the 5% canary (will include metrics thresholds and rollback conditions).

Can we get confirmation on the campaign predictability and the top-10 prompts by EOD Sep 23?

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

---

From: Devon Park <devon@fastcart.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Martin <alex@fastcart.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: tokenstorm, stream-windowing, and SLA split — pilot next steps

Thanks, Marissa — confirmed. Quick answers: 
- Campaigns are a mix: ~60% scheduled promotions (we’ll share the calendar) and ~40% ad-hoc events. Scheduled ones are predictable enough for pre-warm; ad-hoc are the real source of unpredictability.
- We’ll export the top-10 prompt shapes and the 24-hour trace (redacted PII) tonight; expect the upload to s3 by 20:00 PT.
- Temporary pilot diagnostics retention is fine; we’d like logs retained for 7 days.

We’re aligned on the Oct 4 pilot start. Please send the updated sizing proposal and the canary runbook ASAP so the infra team can prep.

Devon Park
Senior Engineering Manager, FastCart
devon@fastcart.ai
